 Inspiration 

 Modern work is rarely just one clean task. 

 You start fixing one bug, notice another issue, remember something else you need to do, open another tab, switch projects, and eventually forget what you were originally trying to finish. 

 The problem is not always knowing what to do. The harder problem is protecting attention, recovering context after interruptions, and turning a large goal into something small enough to start. 

 That inspired us to build SIDEQUEST — an agent-native productivity workspace designed for distraction-prone and nonlinear work styles. 

 Instead of asking users to manage an endless task list, SIDEQUEST is built around one simple idea: 

 
 Stay on the main quest. 
 

 Everything else can be broken down, parked for later, recovered after an interruption, or turned into a structured challenge. 

 We also wanted to explore what productivity software could look like when an AI agent does not need to guess which buttons to click. With WebMCP , SIDEQUEST exposes meaningful application actions directly to compatible agents while keeping the human in control. 

 

 What it does 

 SIDEQUEST combines productivity tools with lightweight game mechanics to make progress easier to understand and more satisfying to continue. 

 Main Quest 

 Users select one important task as their Main Quest . 

 SIDEQUEST then keeps the current goal, progress, blocker, and Next Action visible so the user always knows what to do next. 

 Large tasks can be broken into smaller Quest Steps, including tiny actions that can be completed quickly. 

 If the user gets stuck, Unstuck Mode can help them: 

 
 make the next action smaller, 
 add a tiny step, 
 record a blocker, 
 or temporarily skip a step without abandoning the Quest. 
 

 Side Quest Parking Lot 

 Distractions do not have to become immediate task switches. 

 If another idea appears while working, users can quickly park it as a Side Quest and continue their Main Quest. 

 Side Quests can later be dismissed or promoted into full project Quests. 

 Focus Sessions 

 SIDEQUEST includes timestamp-based Focus Sessions with: 

 
 configurable duration, 
 pause and resume, 
 overtime, 
 current Next Action, 
 Quest progress, 
 and session summaries. 
 

 Focus Sessions connect directly to the user's real Quest rather than being a separate timer. 

 Context Keeper and Resume Me 

 One of the biggest problems with interrupted work is remembering where you stopped. 

 SIDEQUEST can save a lightweight work snapshot containing: 

 
 current Quest, 
 current Step, 
 progress, 
 blocker, 
 Next Action, 
 and an optional note to your future self. 
 

 When the user returns, Resume Me restores their orientation without rolling back newer work. 

 Recovery Quests 

 SIDEQUEST also includes optional non-medical Recovery Quests for: 

 
 water, 
 movement, 
 stretching, 
 eye breaks, 
 bio breaks, 
 and general breaks. 
 

 Recovery is treated as part of sustainable work rather than something that breaks a productivity streak. 

 Gamification 

 Real progress powers the game layer. 

 Users can earn: 

 
 XP, 
 Levels, 
 Achievements, 
 Focus Combos, 
 Skill Tree progress, 
 Challenge rewards, 
 Daily Mission rewards, 
 and Boss Battle progress. 
 

 The system includes anti-farming protection so repeatedly reopening and completing the same Step does not generate unlimited XP. 

 Today's Loadout 

 Users can build a small daily plan with: 

 
 1 Main Mission 
 up to 2 Side Missions 
 optional Recovery goals 
 

 This prevents the daily plan from becoming another overwhelming task list. 

 Boss Battles 

 Large Projects can optionally become Boss Battles . 

 The Boss HP is derived from real Project progress — not an artificial game score. 

 As real Quests are completed, Boss HP decreases until the Project reaches 100%. 

 Challenge Mode 

 Users can create short voluntary challenges such as: 

 
 10 Minute Attack 
 Triple Tap 
 Stay On Target 
 Push the Boss 
 

 Challenges reward completing actual work objectives rather than simply keeping a timer running. 

 Skill Tree 

 SIDEQUEST includes four progression branches: 

 
 Focus 
 Finishing 
 Resilience 
 Recovery 
 

 Skill nodes unlock from real usage patterns such as completing Focus Sessions, finishing Quests, returning after interruptions, and completing Recovery Quests. 

 WebMCP 

 SIDEQUEST exposes structured tools through: 

 document.modelContext 

 A WebMCP-compatible agent can work with the application using actions such as: 

 
 get_current_work_state 
 set_main_quest 
 make_next_action_smaller 
 park_side_quest 
 save_work_context 
 resume_work_context 
 start_focus_session 
 suggest_recovery 
 get_player_state 
 

 These tools operate on the same state and business logic as the human-facing UI . 

 When an agent changes something, the user sees the actual application update immediately. 

 SIDEQUEST currently exposes 28 WebMCP tools with structured schemas, read-only hints where appropriate, validation, execution timing, and visible Agent Activity tracking. 

 

 How we built it 

 SIDEQUEST is a frontend-first, local-first web application. 

 Technology stack 

 
 React 
 TypeScript 
 Vite 
 Tailwind CSS 
 shadcn/ui 
 Framer Motion 
 React Router 
 Lucide React 
 WebMCP 
 localStorage 
 Netlify 
 

 We intentionally kept the hackathon version backend-free. 

 There is: 

 
 no custom AI model, 
 no OpenAI API key, 
 no authentication server, 
 no traditional MCP server, 
 and no cloud database required for the core experience. 
 

 Application state is organized into reusable domain stores and actions for areas such as Quests, Focus Sessions, Recovery, Context, Gamification, Challenges, and Daily Missions. 

 The UI and WebMCP tools both call those same domain actions.
